record.paper_title: The Feynman integral path a Henstock integral: a survey and open problems
record.original_question: For the function space H = { h : R^T × N(T) × I(R^T) → C : |∫_{R^T} h| < ∞ }, what is its size as a vector space? More specifically, can one prove that the cardinality of H is at most the continuum c, and therefore that the vector-space dimension of H is exactly c?

evidence.quote: We consider important to study properties of the function space H = { h : RT × N (T ) × I(RT ) → C : |∫RT h| < ∞ }.
We would like to show that Card(H) ≤ c, then Dim(H) = c.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T = [a,b] \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a compact interval and let $\mathbb{R}^T$ denote the set of all functions $x : T \to \mathbb{R}$ (regarded as paths). Let $N(T)$ denote the collection of finite ordered partitions of $T$ (i.e. finite increasing tuples $a = t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_n = b$), and let $I(\mathbb{R}^T)$ denote a chosen family of "interval-like" subsets of $\mathbb{R}^T$ (cylinder sets determined by finitely many coordinates). Suppose that on $\mathbb{R}^T$ one has fixed a Henstock-type integration scheme so that for a complex-valued function $h$ defined on triples $(x, P, J) \in \mathbb{R}^T \times N(T) \times I(\mathbb{R}^T)$ the symbol $\int_{\mathbb{R}^T} h$ has a precise meaning (as a Henstock limit of Riemann-type sums indexed by partitions $P$ and cylinder sets $J$).

Define the function space
$$H \;=\; \Bigl\{\, h : \mathbb{R}^T \times N(T) \times I(\mathbb{R}^T) \to \mathbb{C} \;:\; \Bigl|\int_{\mathbb{R}^T} h\Bigr| < \infty \,\Bigr\},$$
viewed as a complex vector space under pointwise operations.

Prove or disprove: the cardinality of $H$ satisfies $\mathrm{Card}(H) \le \mathfrak{c}$ (the cardinality of the continuum), and consequently the vector-space dimension of $H$ over $\mathbb{C}$ equals $\mathfrak{c}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on the Feynman path integral as a Henstock integral. No subsequent work resolving the cardinality/dimension question for this specific function space H was located in a brief search, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.claim: The cardinality/dimension question about H is explicitly listed as an open problem.
